sugar.label: Sugar
sugar.what: Sugar is a simple carbohydrate used mainly to provide sweetness and energy.
sugar.why_used: It is added to foods to provide sweetness, improve flavour and contribute to texture.
sugar.health: Sugar provides energy but relatively little micronutritional value. High intake of free or added sugars can increase overall calorie intake.
sugar.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

high fructose corn syrup.label: High Fructose Corn Syrup
high fructose corn syrup.what: High fructose corn syrup is a liquid sweetener made from corn-derived glucose and fructose.
high fructose corn syrup.why_used: It provides sweetness and helps contribute to the texture and moisture of processed foods.
high fructose corn syrup.health: It is a source of added sugar. Its nutritional significance depends mainly on the total amount consumed.
high fructose corn syrup.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

glucose syrup.label: Glucose Syrup
glucose syrup.what: Glucose syrup is a carbohydrate syrup containing glucose and other sugars.
glucose syrup.why_used: It provides sweetness and can improve texture and consistency.
glucose syrup.health: It contributes carbohydrate and calories and is considered a source of added sugar.
glucose syrup.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

fructose.label: Fructose
fructose.what: Fructose is a naturally occurring simple sugar found in fruits and other foods.
fructose.why_used: It is used as a sweetening ingredient.
fructose.health: Fructose contributes energy. Its effect depends on the total amount consumed and the food source.
fructose.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

dextrose.label: Dextrose
dextrose.what: Dextrose is another name commonly used for glucose.
dextrose.why_used: It can provide sweetness, carbohydrate and browning during cooking.
dextrose.health: It contributes carbohydrate and energy and is generally treated as an added sugar when added to foods.
dextrose.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

maltodextrin.label: Maltodextrin
maltodextrin.what: Maltodextrin is a carbohydrate produced by breaking down starch.
maltodextrin.why_used: It can provide bulk, improve texture and act as a carrier for flavours or other ingredients.
maltodextrin.health: It is readily digestible and contributes carbohydrate and calories.
maltodextrin.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

wheat flour.label: Wheat Flour
wheat flour.what: Wheat flour is flour produced by milling wheat grains.
wheat flour.why_used: It provides structure, texture and carbohydrates in baked and cereal-based foods.
wheat flour.health: Whole-wheat flour generally contains more fibre and micronutrients than highly refined flour.
wheat flour.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

whole oats flour.label: Whole Oats Flour
whole oats flour.what: Whole oats flour is produced from whole oat grains and contains the grain's main components.
whole oats flour.why_used: It contributes grain flavour, texture, carbohydrates and dietary fibre.
whole oats flour.health: Oats provide dietary fibre and nutrients; whole oats contain beta-glucan, a soluble fibre.
whole oats flour.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

corn meal.label: Corn Meal
corn meal.what: Corn meal is ground maize used as a cereal-based ingredient.
corn meal.why_used: It contributes texture, flavour and carbohydrates.
corn meal.health: Corn provides carbohydrate and can contribute fibre and micronutrients depending on processing.
corn meal.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

palm oil.label: Palm Oil
palm oil.what: Palm oil is a vegetable oil obtained from the fruit of oil palms.
palm oil.why_used: It contributes fat, texture, mouthfeel and stability to processed foods.
palm oil.health: Palm oil contains a substantial proportion of saturated fat, so the amount consumed contributes to total saturated-fat intake.
palm oil.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

sunflower oil.label: Sunflower Oil
sunflower oil.what: Sunflower oil is a vegetable oil extracted from sunflower seeds.
sunflower oil.why_used: It is used as a cooking and formulation oil and contributes texture and mouthfeel.
sunflower oil.health: Its nutritional profile depends on the type of sunflower oil; it generally contains mostly unsaturated fat.
sunflower oil.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

milk.label: Milk
milk.what: Milk is a dairy ingredient that can provide protein, fat, lactose and minerals.
milk.why_used: Milk ingredients can contribute flavour, texture, protein and nutritional components.
milk.health: Milk provides nutrients such as protein and calcium, but milk is a major food allergen for susceptible individuals.
milk.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

soy.label: Soy
soy.what: Soy is a legume commonly used as a source of protein and as a food ingredient.
soy.why_used: Soy-derived ingredients can provide protein, emulsification, texture or flavour depending on the ingredient.
soy.health: Soy provides protein and other nutrients, but it is a major allergen for susceptible individuals.
soy.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

peanuts.label: Peanuts
peanuts.what: Peanuts are legumes containing protein and fat.
peanuts.why_used: Peanuts and peanut-derived ingredients can provide flavour, texture and fat.
peanuts.health: Peanuts provide protein and unsaturated fats, but they are a major allergen and can cause severe reactions in susceptible people.
peanuts.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

wheat.label: Wheat
wheat.what: Wheat is a cereal grain containing carbohydrates and proteins including gluten proteins.
wheat.why_used: Wheat ingredients provide structure, texture and carbohydrates in many foods.
wheat.health: Wheat is nutritious for many people, but it contains gluten and is relevant to people with wheat allergy or gluten-related disorders.
wheat.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

lecithin.label: Lecithin (INS 322)
lecithin.what: Lecithin is a mixture of phospholipids used as an emulsifier.
lecithin.why_used: It helps ingredients such as water and oil remain evenly mixed and can improve texture and processing.
lecithin.health: Lecithin is widely used as a food emulsifier. The source may be relevant for people with particular allergies.
lecithin.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

mixed tocopherols.label: Mixed Tocopherols (INS 307b)
mixed tocopherols.what: Mixed tocopherols are forms of vitamin E compounds that have antioxidant properties.
mixed tocopherols.why_used: They are used to slow oxidation of fats and oils and help maintain product quality and shelf life.
mixed tocopherols.health: Tocopherols are vitamin E-related compounds. Their nutritional and technological roles depend on the specific tocopherol and amount present.
mixed tocopherols.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

tocopherols.label: Tocopherols (INS 307b)
tocopherols.what: Tocopherols are vitamin E-related compounds with antioxidant activity.
tocopherols.why_used: They help protect fats and oils from oxidation.
tocopherols.health: Tocopherols are related to vitamin E and are commonly used in foods as antioxidants.
tocopherols.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

monosodium glutamate.label: MSG (INS 621)
monosodium glutamate.what: Monosodium glutamate is the sodium salt of glutamic acid and is used as a flavour enhancer.
monosodium glutamate.why_used: It enhances savoury and umami flavours.
monosodium glutamate.health: MSG is permitted as a food additive in regulated amounts. Some individuals report sensitivity to large amounts.
monosodium glutamate.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

sodium benzoate.label: Sodium Benzoate (INS 211)
sodium benzoate.what: Sodium benzoate is a preservative derived from benzoic acid.
sodium benzoate.why_used: It helps inhibit the growth of certain microorganisms and extends shelf life.
sodium benzoate.health: It is widely used as a preservative within regulated limits.
sodium benzoate.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

potassium sorbate.label: Potassium Sorbate (INS 202)
potassium sorbate.what: Potassium sorbate is the potassium salt of sorbic acid.
potassium sorbate.why_used: It helps prevent the growth of moulds and yeasts.
potassium sorbate.health: It is widely used as a preservative within regulated limits.
potassium sorbate.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

citric acid.label: Citric Acid (INS 330)
citric acid.what: Citric acid is an organic acid naturally found in citrus fruits.
citric acid.why_used: It is used to provide acidity, balance flavour and help control product pH.
citric acid.health: Citric acid is commonly used in foods as an acidity regulator.
citric acid.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

ascorbic acid.label: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C, INS 300)
ascorbic acid.what: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C and can also act as an antioxidant in foods.
ascorbic acid.why_used: It can help protect food from oxidation and may also be used for nutritional fortification.
ascorbic acid.health: Vitamin C is an essential nutrient involved in normal immune function, collagen formation and antioxidant activity.
ascorbic acid.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

sodium bicarbonate.label: Sodium Bicarbonate (INS 500)
sodium bicarbonate.what: Sodium bicarbonate is a chemical leavening agent commonly known as baking soda.
sodium bicarbonate.why_used: It releases carbon dioxide under suitable conditions, helping baked foods rise.
sodium bicarbonate.health: It contributes sodium to the food. Its significance depends on the amount used.
sodium bicarbonate.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

caramel.label: Caramel Colour (INS 150)
caramel.what: Caramel colour is a brown colouring substance produced by controlled heating of carbohydrates.
caramel.why_used: It is used to give foods a characteristic brown colour.
caramel.health: Different caramel colour classes have different specifications and permitted uses.
caramel.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

tartrazine.label: Tartrazine (INS 102)
tartrazine.what: Tartrazine is a synthetic yellow food colour.
tartrazine.why_used: It is used to provide or enhance yellow colour in foods.
tartrazine.health: It is a regulated food colour. Certain sensitive individuals may experience reactions.
tartrazine.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

sunset yellow.label: Sunset Yellow FCF (INS 110)
sunset yellow.what: Sunset Yellow FCF is a synthetic orange-yellow food colour.
sunset yellow.why_used: It is used to give foods an orange or yellow appearance.
sunset yellow.health: It is a regulated food colour. Some individuals may be sensitive to certain food colours.
sunset yellow.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

allura red.label: Allura Red AC (INS 129)
allura red.what: Allura Red AC is a synthetic red food colour.
allura red.why_used: It is used to provide a red colour to foods and beverages.
allura red.health: It is a regulated food colour. Responses to food colours can vary between individuals.
allura red.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

disodium inosinate.label: Disodium Inosinate (INS 631)
disodium inosinate.what: Disodium inosinate is a flavour enhancer derived from inosine monophosphate.
disodium inosinate.why_used: It enhances savoury and umami flavours and is often used with other flavour enhancers.
disodium inosinate.health: It is used in regulated food applications. People following specific dietary restrictions may wish to check its source.
disodium inosinate.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

disodium guanylate.label: Disodium Guanylate (INS 627)
disodium guanylate.what: Disodium guanylate is a flavour enhancer.
disodium guanylate.why_used: It contributes to savoury and umami flavour.
disodium guanylate.health: It is used as a regulated food additive. Its significance depends on the amount consumed.
disodium guanylate.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

milk solids.label: Milk Solids
milk solids.what: Milk solids are the non-water components of milk, including proteins, lactose and minerals.
milk solids.why_used: They can provide dairy flavour, protein, texture and solids to processed foods.
milk solids.health: Milk solids provide nutrients but are relevant to people with milk allergy or lactose-related dietary concerns.
milk solids.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

cocoa solids.label: Cocoa Solids
cocoa solids.what: Cocoa solids are the non-fat components of processed cocoa beans.
cocoa solids.why_used: They provide chocolate flavour, colour and characteristic cocoa compounds.
cocoa solids.health: Cocoa contains naturally occurring compounds such as polyphenols. The overall nutritional profile depends on the amount and other ingredients in the product.
cocoa solids.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

iodised salt.label: Iodised Salt
iodised salt.what: Iodised salt is salt fortified with iodine.
iodised salt.why_used: It enhances flavour and provides iodine.
iodised salt.health: Iodine is an essential nutrient needed for normal thyroid function. Salt also contributes sodium, so total intake matters.
iodised salt.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

natural flavour.label: Natural Flavour
natural flavour.what: Natural flavour refers to flavouring substances obtained from natural source materials and used to provide flavour.
natural flavour.why_used: It is used to provide or enhance the characteristic flavour of the product.
natural flavour.health: The term covers many different flavouring substances, so the specific composition depends on the formulation and applicable food regulations.
natural flavour.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

cocoa butter.label: Cocoa Butter
cocoa butter.what: Cocoa butter is the natural fat pressed out of cocoa beans, solid at room temperature and melting near body temperature.
cocoa butter.why_used: Gives chocolate its smooth melt and texture.
cocoa butter.health: A saturated fat, similar in effect to other solid vegetable fats.
cocoa butter.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

coconut oil.label: Coconut Oil
coconut oil.what: Coconut oil is a fat pressed from the dried flesh of coconuts, solid at room temperature.
coconut oil.why_used: Adds richness and a distinct flavour, and keeps baked goods moist.
coconut oil.health: Very high in saturated fat compared with most other cooking oils.
coconut oil.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

vegetable oil.label: Vegetable Oil
vegetable oil.what: A general term for oil pressed from one or more plant sources, such as soybean, sunflower or rapeseed.
vegetable oil.why_used: Used for frying, moisture and texture.
vegetable oil.health: The label not naming the specific plant source makes it hard to know the fat profile.
vegetable oil.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

canola oil.label: Canola Oil
canola oil.what: An oil pressed from rapeseed, bred to be low in the compounds that make older rapeseed oil taste bitter.
canola oil.why_used: A neutral-tasting oil used for cooking or frying.
canola oil.health: Relatively low in saturated fat compared with palm or coconut oil.
canola oil.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

olive oil.label: Olive Oil
olive oil.why_used: Adds flavour and is used for cooking or as a finishing oil.
olive oil.health: Mostly unsaturated fat, generally considered a healthier cooking oil choice.
olive oil.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

rice flour.label: Rice Flour
rice flour.what: Flour milled from rice grains, naturally free of gluten.
rice flour.why_used: Used for texture, thickening, or as a gluten-free base.
rice flour.health: A source of carbohydrate; naturally gluten-free.
rice flour.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

oat flour.label: Oat Flour
oat flour.what: Oats that have been rolled, milled or ground into flour or flakes.
oat flour.why_used: Adds texture, fibre and a mild, nutty flavour.
oat flour.health: A source of dietary fibre, particularly beta-glucan.
oat flour.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

barley malt.label: Barley Malt
barley malt.what: A syrup or powder made by sprouting and drying barley, then extracting the sugars produced.
barley malt.why_used: Adds a toasty sweetness and helps with browning.
barley malt.health: Contains natural sugars and, since it comes from barley, gluten.
barley malt.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

cornstarch.label: Cornstarch
cornstarch.what: A fine starch extracted from corn kernels.
cornstarch.why_used: Used to thicken sauces or as an anti-caking agent between food pieces.
cornstarch.health: A refined carbohydrate with little nutritional value beyond energy.
cornstarch.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

brown sugar.label: Brown Sugar
brown sugar.what: Refined sugar with molasses added back in, giving it colour and a caramel-like flavour.
brown sugar.why_used: For sweetness and a deeper flavour than white sugar.
brown sugar.health: Nutritionally very similar to white sugar — still an added sugar.
brown sugar.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

invert sugar.label: Invert Sugar
invert sugar.what: A liquid sugar made by splitting ordinary sugar into its two component sugars, which resists crystallising.
invert sugar.why_used: Keeps baked goods and sweets soft and prevents sugar from turning grainy.
invert sugar.health: An added sugar, nutritionally similar to table sugar.
invert sugar.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

stevia.label: Stevia
stevia.what: A sweetener extracted from the leaves of the stevia plant, hundreds of times sweeter than sugar by weight.
stevia.why_used: Adds sweetness with little or no calories.
stevia.health: A plant-derived, non-sugar sweetener; some people notice a mild bitter or liquorice-like aftertaste.
stevia.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

sucralose.label: Sucralose
sucralose.what: An artificial sweetener made from sugar through a chemical process, roughly 600 times sweeter than sugar.
sucralose.why_used: Adds sweetness with essentially no calories.
sucralose.health: Passes through the body largely unabsorbed. Considered safe by major food regulators within set limits.
sucralose.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

aspartame.label: Aspartame
aspartame.what: An artificial sweetener made from two amino acids, around 200 times sweeter than sugar.
aspartame.why_used: Adds sweetness with almost no calories.
aspartame.health: Not suitable for people with the rare condition phenylketonuria (PKU), since it contains phenylalanine.
aspartame.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

sorbitol.label: Sorbitol
sorbitol.what: A sugar alcohol, naturally found in some fruits, used as a lower-calorie sweetener.
sorbitol.why_used: Adds sweetness and keeps foods moist, with fewer calories than sugar.
sorbitol.health: Can have a laxative effect if eaten in large amounts.
sorbitol.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

xylitol.label: Xylitol
xylitol.what: A sugar alcohol, often derived from birch or corn, roughly as sweet as sugar with fewer calories.
xylitol.why_used: Adds sweetness and is often used in sugar-free gum and mints.
xylitol.health: Can cause digestive upset in large amounts, and is toxic to dogs.
xylitol.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

erythritol.label: Erythritol
erythritol.what: A sugar alcohol that occurs naturally in small amounts in some fruits, used as a near-zero-calorie sweetener.
erythritol.why_used: Adds sweetness with minimal calories and little effect on blood sugar.
erythritol.health: Generally well tolerated, though large amounts can cause digestive discomfort in some people.
erythritol.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

xanthan gum.label: Xanthan Gum
xanthan gum.what: A thickener produced by fermenting sugar with a specific bacteria, then purifying the result.
xanthan gum.why_used: Thickens liquids and keeps mixtures from separating, even in tiny amounts.
xanthan gum.health: Generally considered safe; very large amounts can have a mild laxative effect.
xanthan gum.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

guar gum.label: Guar Gum
guar gum.what: A thickener made from the ground seeds of the guar bean.
guar gum.why_used: Thickens and stabilises foods, and can add a sense of fibre.
guar gum.health: A source of soluble fibre; can cause bloating if consumed in large amounts.
guar gum.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

pectin.label: Pectin
pectin.what: A natural thickener found in the cell walls of fruit, especially apples and citrus peel.
pectin.why_used: Sets jams and jellies and thickens fruit-based products.
pectin.health: A soluble fibre. Generally well tolerated.
pectin.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

gelatin.label: Gelatin
gelatin.what: A protein extracted by boiling animal bones, skin or connective tissue.
gelatin.why_used: Sets liquids into a gel, used in sweets, marshmallows and some desserts.
gelatin.health: Not suitable for vegetarians or vegans, since it's made from animal tissue.
gelatin.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

agar agar.label: Agar Agar
agar agar.what: A gelling agent extracted from red seaweed, often used as a plant-based substitute for gelatin.
agar agar.why_used: Sets liquids into a gel without using animal products.
agar agar.health: A source of fibre from seaweed. Generally well tolerated.
agar agar.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

carrageenan.label: Carrageenan
carrageenan.what: A thickener extracted from red seaweed.
carrageenan.why_used: Keeps dairy and plant-milk products smooth and prevents ingredients from separating.
carrageenan.health: Approved by major food regulators; some people choose to avoid it as a precaution, though evidence of harm at food-use levels is limited.
carrageenan.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

whey protein.label: Whey Protein
whey protein.what: A protein separated from milk during cheese-making, dried into a powder.
whey protein.why_used: Boosts the protein content of a food or drink.
whey protein.health: A dairy-derived protein — not suitable for those with a milk allergy or who are vegan.
whey protein.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

soy protein.label: Soy Protein
soy protein.what: Protein extracted or textured from soybeans, used as a meat substitute or protein booster.
soy protein.why_used: Adds protein and can mimic the texture of meat in vegetarian products.
soy protein.health: A common allergen. A complete plant protein otherwise.
soy protein.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

hydrolyzed vegetable protein.label: Hydrolyzed Vegetable Protein
hydrolyzed vegetable protein.what: Plant protein broken down chemically into its component amino acids, which include natural glutamate.
hydrolyzed vegetable protein.why_used: Adds a strong savoury, meaty flavour to processed foods.
hydrolyzed vegetable protein.health: Naturally high in glutamate, similar in effect to added MSG.
hydrolyzed vegetable protein.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

yeast extract.label: Yeast Extract
yeast extract.what: A savoury paste or powder made by breaking down yeast cells, naturally rich in glutamate.
yeast extract.why_used: Adds a strong savoury flavour, similar to the effect of added MSG.
yeast extract.health: Naturally contains glutamate. Some brands are also a source of B vitamins.
yeast extract.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

gum arabic.label: Gum Arabic
gum arabic.what: A gum harvested from the sap of acacia trees.
gum arabic.why_used: Stabilises foams and prevents sugar from crystallising in sweets and drinks.
gum arabic.health: A soluble fibre, generally well tolerated.
gum arabic.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

bha.label: BHA
bha.what: A synthetic antioxidant that stops fats in food from reacting with oxygen and turning rancid.
bha.why_used: Extends shelf life by keeping fats from spoiling.
bha.health: Regulatory bodies set strict limits on how much can be used; some people prefer to avoid it as a precaution.
bha.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

bht.label: BHT
bht.what: A synthetic antioxidant, closely related to BHA, used to keep fats from going rancid.
bht.health: Used within regulatory limits; some people choose to avoid it as a precaution.
bht.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

tbhq.label: TBHQ
tbhq.what: A synthetic antioxidant added to oils and fried snacks to slow them turning rancid.
tbhq.why_used: Extends the shelf life of oils and fatty foods.
tbhq.health: Used within set regulatory limits; considered one of the additives some shoppers prefer to limit.
tbhq.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

titanium dioxide.label: Titanium Dioxide
titanium dioxide.what: A bright white mineral pigment used to make foods look whiter or more opaque.
titanium dioxide.why_used: Purely for appearance — it has no taste or nutritional role.
titanium dioxide.health: Banned as a food additive in the EU since 2022 over unresolved safety questions; still permitted in many other countries.
titanium dioxide.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

silicon dioxide.label: Silicon Dioxide
silicon dioxide.what: A fine mineral powder used to stop powdered ingredients clumping together.
silicon dioxide.why_used: Keeps powders like spice mixes or instant soups free-flowing.
silicon dioxide.health: Passes through the body largely unabsorbed. Considered safe at typical food-use levels.
silicon dioxide.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

calcium carbonate.label: Calcium Carbonate
calcium carbonate.what: A mineral, essentially food-grade chalk, used as a calcium source or acidity regulator.
calcium carbonate.why_used: Fortifies foods with calcium, or controls acidity.
calcium carbonate.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

ferrous sulfate.label: Iron (Ferrous Sulfate)
ferrous sulfate.what: An iron compound added to fortify foods, commonly used in flour fortification programmes.
ferrous sulfate.why_used: Adds iron to help prevent iron-deficiency anaemia at a population level.
ferrous sulfate.health: A dietary mineral. Large excess intake from supplements (not typically from food) can be harmful.
ferrous sulfate.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

folic acid.label: Folic Acid
folic acid.what: The synthetic form of vitamin B9, often added to flour and cereals.
folic acid.why_used: Fortification to help prevent birth defects at a population level.
folic acid.health: An essential vitamin at normal intake levels.
folic acid.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

niacin.label: Niacin
niacin.what: Vitamin B3, often added to fortify flour and cereal products.
niacin.health: An essential vitamin at normal intake levels.
niacin.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

vinegar.label: Vinegar
vinegar.what: A sour liquid made by fermenting alcohol into acetic acid.
vinegar.why_used: Adds tang, controls acidity, and helps preserve food.
vinegar.health: A normal food ingredient in the amounts typically used.
vinegar.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

baking powder.label: Baking Powder
baking powder.what: A mix of baking soda and a mild acid, which reacts with liquid or heat to release gas bubbles.
baking powder.why_used: Makes baked goods rise without needing yeast.
baking powder.health: A normal food ingredient in the amounts typically used.
baking powder.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

cream of tartar.label: Cream Of Tartar
cream of tartar.what: An acidic byproduct of winemaking, used to stabilise whipped egg whites and help baked goods rise.
cream of tartar.why_used: Stabilises foams and activates baking soda.
cream of tartar.health: A normal food ingredient in the amounts typically used.
cream of tartar.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

vanilla.label: Vanilla
vanilla.what: A flavouring derived from vanilla pods, or a synthetic version (vanillin) that mimics the same taste.
vanilla.why_used: Adds a warm, sweet aroma and flavour.
vanilla.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

cinnamon.label: Cinnamon
cinnamon.what: A spice made from the dried inner bark of the cinnamon tree.
cinnamon.health: A normal spice at food-use levels.
cinnamon.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

black pepper.label: Black Pepper
black pepper.what: A spice made from dried, unripe peppercorns.
black pepper.why_used: Adds heat and a sharp, warm flavour.
black pepper.health: A normal spice at food-use levels.
black pepper.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

turmeric.label: Turmeric
turmeric.what: A spice from the root of the turmeric plant, also used as a natural yellow colouring.
turmeric.why_used: Adds colour and an earthy flavour.
turmeric.health: A normal spice at food-use levels.
turmeric.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

garlic powder.label: Garlic Powder
garlic powder.what: Fresh garlic that has been dried and ground into a powder.
garlic powder.why_used: Adds garlic flavour with a longer shelf life than fresh garlic.
garlic powder.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

onion powder.label: Onion Powder
onion powder.what: Dried, ground onion, used as a convenient seasoning.
onion powder.why_used: Adds onion flavour without fresh onion's moisture or shelf life.
onion powder.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

paprika.label: Paprika
paprika.what: A spice made from dried, ground sweet or mild peppers.
paprika.why_used: Adds colour and a mild, sweet pepper flavour.
paprika.health: A normal spice at food-use levels.
paprika.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

egg.label: Egg
egg.what: Whole egg, egg white or egg yolk, usually dried into a powder for use in packaged food.
egg.why_used: Binds ingredients together and adds structure, richness or a glossy finish.
egg.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

yeast.label: Yeast
yeast.what: A living microorganism that ferments sugars and releases carbon dioxide gas.
yeast.health: A normal ingredient in baked goods.
yeast.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

malt extract.label: Malt Extract
malt extract.what: A thick syrup made by extracting the sugars from sprouted, dried barley.
malt extract.health: Contains natural sugars, and gluten from the barley.
malt extract.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

beta carotene.label: Beta Carotene
beta carotene.what: A natural orange-yellow pigment, found in carrots and many other plants, and also converted by the body into vitamin A.
beta carotene.why_used: Used as a natural food colouring.
beta carotene.health: Generally considered a benign, naturally occurring colouring.
beta carotene.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

annatto.label: Annatto
annatto.what: A natural orange-red colouring extracted from the seeds of the achiote tree.
annatto.why_used: Used as a natural alternative to synthetic colours.
annatto.health: Rarely, some people report a sensitivity to it.
annatto.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

sodium nitrite.label: Sodium Nitrite
sodium nitrite.what: A preservative used mainly in cured and processed meats to stop bacterial growth and fix a pink colour.
sodium nitrite.why_used: Prevents the growth of bacteria that cause botulism, and cures meat.
sodium nitrite.health: Regulated within strict limits. Frequently discussed in relation to processed-meat consumption.
sodium nitrite.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.

calcium propionate.label: Calcium Propionate
calcium propionate.what: A preservative commonly used in bread to stop mould growing.
calcium propionate.why_used: Extends the shelf life of baked goods.
calcium propionate.health: Used within regulatory limits; considered low-risk by major food safety bodies.
calcium propionate.quantity: The exact quantity is not stated on the label.
